To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute liver intoxication during bone fracture healing in mice is characterized by decreased calcium and phosphate deposition in the regenerating bone tissue and decreased collagen formation.

in the process of bone regeneration in mice with acute hepated intoxication, the formation of mineral components of the bone decreases significantly and the formation of organic components to a lesser degree.

the accumulation of calcium and phosphate in regenerating bones decreases significantly during the post-traumatic period in 60 male CBA mice, while the formation of organic bone components is less affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of the acute hepatic intoxicication on the process of fracture healing in CBA mice.
the role of the liver in bone and muscle regeneration.
the role of creatine in the process of fracture healing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute hepatic intoxicication does not affect the healing of a bone fracture.

the healing process of the fracture in mice with acute hepetic intoxication was significantly delayed, which was associated with a decrease in the intensity of the accumulation of calcium, phosphate, and collagen in bone tissue.
the process of regeneration in the bone tissue of mice with acute hepetic intoxication is slower than in healthy animals, but the process of muscle regeneration proceeds normally.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accumulation of calcium, phosphate, and collagen in bones of mice with acute hepated intoxication during the healing of the shin fracture was lower than in control mice.
the formation of bone tissue during the posttrauma period is impaired in mice with hepatic intoxication.

the formation of bone and muscle tissues in the posttraumatic regeneration period is characterized by a decrease in the intensity of calcium and phosphorus accumulation in bone tissue and creatine accumulation in muscle tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of acute hepatic intoxicication during the post-traumatic period in mice with a fracture of the shin bone leads to the development of osteoporosis, which is manifested by a decrease in the accumulation of calcium, phosphate, and organic components in bone tissues.
the accumulation of calcium, phosphate, and collagen in the bone of mice with acute hepetic intoxication during fracture healing was reduced.
the accumulation of calcium and phosphate in regenerating bone is more sensitive to the toxic effect than the formation of organic components.
